criteria.text: The participant is ≥ 18 years old (or ≥ the legal age within the country if it is older than 18 years).
The participant has a histologically confirmed MSI-H or dMMR metastatic or locally advanced solid tumor by local testing or central testing.
Tumor tissue (formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded sample) archival block must be available. Participants without archived tumor tissue may enroll by undergoing tumor biopsy before dosing.
The participant's disease is measurable as defined by Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors Version 1.1 (RECIST 1.1).
The participant has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance (ECOG) status of 0-1.
The participant has adequate organ function as defined in the protocol.
The participant has a primary central nervous system (CNS) tumor.
The participant has impaired cardiac function or clinically significant cardiac disease.
The participant had major surgery within 28 days of trial day 1.

The participant received antitumor therapy (chemotherapy, antibody therapy, molecular targeted therapy, hormonal therapy, or investigational agent) within 21 days of first dose of trial treatment, unless anti-tumor therapy is a therapy with 5 times the half-life being shorter than 21 days (in this case, enrollment may be allowed with washout from prior therapy of < 21 days).
The participant received radiation therapy within 28 days of the first dose of trial treatment (or local or focal radiotherapy with palliative intent within 14 days of the first dose).

The participant has gastrointestinal tract disease causing the inability to take per os (PO) medication, malabsorption syndrome, requirement for intravenous (IV) alimentation, or uncontrolled inflammatory gastrointestinal disease (eg, Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis).

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: These questions are about the trial "AMG 436 as Monotherapy and Combination Therapy in Participants With MSI-H/dMMR Solid Tumors". Your earlier answers already covered 3 of its rules. I'll ask about the rest of its rules one at a time. You can skip any question, and "I don't know" is always fine.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To confirm, are you 18 years of age or older?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: Yes, I am 63 years old.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had recent blood tests (like a complete blood count, chemistry panel, and coagulation tests) that showed your organ function is adequate?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I'm not sure about the specific details of my recent blood tests or organ function results. I'd need to check with my doctor for that information.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with a primary tumor in the central nervous system (brain or spinal cord)?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, nothing in my brain, thankfully. I know the cancer has spread to my bones and lymph nodes, but my brain is clear.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. To clarify, have you ever been diagnosed with a primary tumor in the central nervous system (brain or spinal cord)?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't. As I mentioned, the cancer has spread to my bones and lymph nodes, but there is nothing in my brain or spinal cord.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with a heart condition or have you had any issues with your heart function, such as heart failure or irregular heartbeat?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't had any heart issues like heart failure or irregular heartbeat in the last six months.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you ever been diagnosed with any other heart conditions or issues with your heart function, such as impaired cardiac function or clinically significant cardiac disease?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't had any other heart conditions. I've been clear on that front.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you had any major surgery in the last 28 days?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't had any major surgery recently.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have you received any cancer treatments (like chemotherapy, targeted therapy, or hormonal therapy) in the last 21 days?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't had any cancer treatments in the last 21 days. My last treatment was Keytruda with chemotherapy, but that was a while ago.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Have you received any radiation therapy in the last 28 days?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No radiation. I haven't had any radiation therapy recently.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you have any gastrointestinal conditions, such as Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis, that make it difficult to take oral medication or absorb nutrients?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I don't have Crohn's or ulcerative colitis. I don't have any other autoimmune diseases that require immune-calming medicine either.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you have any other GI conditions that make it hard to take pills, cause nutrient absorption issues, require IV feeding, or involve uncontrolled inflammation?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: I don't have any other GI conditions that cause those issues. I'm up and about and can still read and walk, so I don't think I have problems absorbing nutrients or needing IV feeding.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you, that's all my questions. Your record for this trial is ready, for you and your oncologist. They and the trial team decide whether it is right for you.
